summary: I reviewed 00e301b and 741350c, and the fix is correct. What runner.ts keeps for a finished session now belongs to one attempt (the row's name, its session id and the registry's start), and the runner reads again once the transcript's mtime is past the read. That holds for both closeouts and usage, domain.ts is untouched, and nothing outside the package changed. The new tests fail against the pre-fix runner and against a runner with the mtime check removed. The engine suite and typecheck pass (215 of 218 tests, 0 failures). I found two small problems, neither worth another round: the README and a code comment state an unproven cause as fact, and one test assertion can't tell the retry's usage from the first try's.

findings.what: The README says as fact that "A `view` saw the session listed final thirty seconds before its `StructuredOutput`", and the runner.ts comment at line 379 says the same ("some thirty seconds before"). Nobody recorded that: open-issues.md (around line 278) says the pin was taken between 22:53:25.9Z and 22:53:50.4Z, "at least ten seconds before the statement", and calls it "the reading the evidence allows, not a measurement". The request said the cause is not known and asked to say only what the code allows. As written, a reader of the README or the code takes an unconfirmed guess, with a made-up number, as the known cause, and may stop looking at the other ways a final sighting reaches the runner. The wording should match open-issues: the code allows this, and it was not observed.

The final usage assertion, 'only the responses since its own start', expects {turns 2, toolCalls 2, inputTokens 200, outputTokens 10}. That is exactly the usage the first try recorded at line 110, so it cannot tell the retry's own count from the first try's count carried over, which is the incident's usage failure. Checked by mutation: with usage pinned by session id for good, as before the fix, and the intermediate view step (lines 122-123) removed, this test passes. The refusal rests only on the view assertion at line 123, plus test 2. If the retry wrote a different number of responses (say 3), the recorded end would refuse the carried-over count by itself.

findings.what: This assertion checks almost nothing. `get` parses the response with `res.json()`, so no value in `shown` is the same object as `first`. `shown.indexOf(first)` is therefore -1, and `shown.slice(-1)` checks only the last value. So 'from the first answer on, never nothing' is never really tested: if the section went blank for a moment between the placeholder and the new answer, the test would still pass. The regression that matters (no placeholder) is still caught by the `meanwhile` assertion above it. To check what it claims, find the first index where the data is deep-equal to `first` (e.g. `shown.findIndex((d) => d !== undefined)`).

`touchedSummary` adds up `+a −r` over every branch it reads, but a follower in its own worktree starts from its parent's branch (`runner.ts:600`). So the Factory card shows implement's lines twice, e.g. `+1958` for 979 lines of work. When Claude Code takes the words, the engine's transcript emits them as an event of their own: a `kind: 'system'` event whose text is the words, for a working session (agent-engine/src/runner.ts:343), or an `isMeta` line with Claude Code's wrapper around them, for an idle one. `foldTranscript` draws either as a system marker (transcript.ts:103-105), and `withSaid` keeps that marker and adds a "You said, while it ran" bubble from the journal. `onSuccess` always calls `setText('')`, but the textarea stays enabled while the POST is pending. That POST observes `claude agents` twice (once in `say()`'s `e.view`, once inside `Engine.say`) and writes to a socket, so it takes a noticeable moment. Someone who sends one message and starts typing the next before the 202 comes back loses what they typed. Clear the box only if it still holds the words that were sent, e.g. `setText((now) => (now === words ? '' : now))` using the mutation's variables, or disable the field while `send.isPending`.

findings.what: `presetOf` looks up a workflow name on a card among the api's own repository's workflows, whatever repository the card names; `inbox.tsx:275` never passes it `entry.repo`. Take the card `wf inbox add "Cache the views" --repo /code/other --workflow dev` writes (`workflow: dev`, `repo: /code/other`) while the api serves a repository that also has a `dev`. The start form preselects the api's `dev`, so Start sends `{workflow: 'dev', from: 'repo', card}`. `folderOf` resolves that to `<api repo>/workflows/dev`, and the run gets that folder on `/code/other`. `wf start <inbox>/<card>.md` would run `/code/other/workflows/dev` (`workflowFolder(card.workflow, inboxDir(), card.repo)`). So clicking Start as preset runs a different workflow than the card names, and all that shows it is the small 'from …' path under the button. The api already handles this when filing: `filingOf` writes the folder path for a card about another repository because "its name would be looked for where it is not". The start preset ignores the same rule. features.md's 'What it leaves' describes this preset, but that is no reason to pick the wrong workflow: when the card names a repository other than the api's (`GET /api/repository`), preselect nothing and show the `data-unlisted` note, saying which repository the name belongs to. The web tests only call `presetOf` without a repository, so nothing covers this case.

summary: Reviewed the five commits against 242f9b1. Items 1, 2, 3 and 5 do what was asked; `npx turbo run test --force` passes in all 4 packages and typecheck is clean. Item 4 has a regression: a run started `--after` a parent whose result was merged by hand at ship's gate can never start, because the approval is refused and the only exit offered (`wf cancel`) makes the parent never ship. `wf decide` also still says 'waiting on you: ship' while `wf ls` says nothing waits.

findings.what: A child run waits for ever on a hand-merged parent. A run started with `wf start --after P` starts only when P's `decision` is `shipped`, and `decision` never calls a run shipped while its ending waits at its gate (`awaitingApproval` guard around line 3077; pinned by run.test.ts "a run at its ending step's gate is never shipped … whatever git says"). Before this change, a person whose parent's result was merged by hand could `wf approve P ship`: ship ran, found the branch already merged and signed off, ship was no longer `awaiting approval`, the branch was on the base with commits past it, and P read `shipped`, so the child started. Now `approvalRefusal` refuses that approval and its only suggestion is `wf cancel P`. A cancelled run never ships, so the child's `wf decide` says 'P was cancelled … yours to resolve: wf cancel <child>, or start the work again without --after P'. The refusal's 'Nothing waits on you' is false whenever a run waits on P. Either let an ending that has not run, whose result git has with commits past the base, read as shipped, or leave the gate approvable when a run waits on it (and word the refusal and note accordingly). No test covers a child of a hand-merged parent.

`wf decide P` for a run at ship's gate whose branch was merged by hand still prints 'AWAITING APPROVAL, waiting on you: ship — this workflow's ending, at its gate: nothing of it has run, and your approval is what runs it', a few lines above 'branch wf/…/implement is on main'. At the same moment `wf ls` says nothing waits on you and `wf approve P ship` is refused. That is the same kind of disagreement item 3 fixed (a screen offering a command the verb refuses). The CLI already has the branch standings in hand (line 732), so it can leave such an ending out of `unrun` and print the on-base line and `wf cancel` (or whatever finding 1 settles on) without touching `decision`'s kind. ship.test.ts calls `decide` only after the cancel, so nothing tests this screen before it.

The frontmatter comment and both READMEs say the deny list covers 'everything that moves or throws away what is in a person's checkout', but two ordinary commands, not alternate spellings, are not denied. `git pull` fetches and merges into the person's checkout, and `git pull . wf/<run>/implement` merges a run's result branch, which is the one act this fence exists to stop. `git restore <path>` throws away uncommitted work exactly as `git checkout -- <path>` does, and that one is denied. Add `Bash(git pull:*)` and `Bash(git restore:*)`, with the matching entries in supervisor.test.ts's GIT_DENIED, or narrow the claim.

summary: Reviewed the supervisor change: `slot: none` through the parser, `validate`, `slotNeed`/`runAdmitted`/`takesNoSlot` and the pass's count, the `workflows/supervisor/` folder, the `workspace: main` brief fixes, and the tests. Suite and typecheck are green and the slot machinery is correct and honestly tested — every caller updated, refusals tested on `err.message` at shipped defaults, and the never-ending path exercised on disk. Four findings, all about how the session behaves once the operator actually starts it: it can block the very `ship` it approves, it silently halves the `claude` session pool, its per-pass cost grows with every answer, and one README bullet is now untrue.

findings.what: The supervisor is told it may write CLAUDE.md / features.md / plan-hold-the-bar.md in the repository's own checkout, and is given no rule about when. `workflows/dev/ship.md:21-23` — which runs in that same checkout — says `git status --porcelain` must say nothing, and otherwise signs off `blocked` with "somebody else is working in this checkout". So the sequence the brief actively encourages (diagnose a stall → "write it down" → `wf approve <run> ship`) leaves an uncommitted file in the tree for exactly the tick that files the approved ship, and the ship refuses. Worse when the supervisor writes a file and then signs off `blocked` to ask a question: the tree stays dirty for as long as the person takes to answer, which is the window an earlier yes's ship gets filed in. The brief covers the opposite direction (line 110: don't touch a checkout mid-merge) but not this one. It needs "commit what you wrote, by path, before any `wf approve`, and never sign off with the checkout dirty". Related: the recipe given is `git commit <path>`, which fails on a path git does not yet track, and the brief forbids `git add -A` without offering `git add <path>`.

"It still takes a session slot, like every session (`WF_MAX_CONCURRENT`)" understates the cost at shipped defaults. `ceilings()` (runner.ts:361) defaults `sessions` to 2, counted per harness pool; `supervise.md` is `harness: claude`, and so are `dev`'s implement, review and ship. The supervisor's loop is `wf ls` → `sleep 60` → `wf ls`, so its session is *running* nearly all the time and holds one of the two `claude` slots continuously — it only frees one in the gap between signing off `blocked` and being answered. The operator who starts the first run therefore drops the board from two concurrent claude sessions to one, and `slot: none` (which exempts it from `WF_MAX_RUNS`) does nothing about it. Neither the README, supervise.md nor features.md's "What it leaves" says this, so the first symptom is a board that has mysteriously halved. It wants a sentence naming the default of 2 and the recommendation to raise `WF_MAX_CONCURRENT` before starting the supervisor.

`taskPhases` reads `e.view` for every earlier try of every step, on every pass, with no cache across passes — and `advance`, `list`, `decide` and `runSlots` each call it. For every other workflow the try count is bounded by `retries:` and a person's patience; the supervisor is the first step designed to be answered without limit, and each answer appends a try (the new test asserts `tries.length === 5` after five). So the supervisor's run costs N+1 journal reads per `wf up` tick (every 4000ms) and per `wf ls`, growing linearly and for ever: ~100 reads/tick after a hundred answers, ~500 after five hundred, plus a run record whose `tries` array is rewritten each pass and a `timeline` the board renders over all of them. features.md's "Nothing caps a step answered many times, and there was nothing to lift" answers the question §9 asked about a *cap*, but this is the thing the package actually lacks for a step that never ends, and it is neither measured nor listed under "What it leaves". The lever is visible: earlier tries' views are read to total `stepSpend` against `budget:`, and `supervise.md` sets no `budget:` — so for this step every one of those reads buys nothing.

"**The step is told both ways**, on its brief, beside the closeout contract (`artifactsContract`): put a file in `<dir>` and name it by absolute path, or leave it in the workspace and name it by its path from the workspace root." This is no longer true after the `artifactsContract(dir, inMain)` change: a `workspace: main` step is now told exactly one way, and `run.test.ts` asserts the brief does *not* contain "Or leave it in this workspace". A reader of this section — or the next agent writing an ending step — would tell a `workspace: main` step to leave a file in the workspace and have it silently not collected. The same sentence is in docs/features.md:1128. The README gained a supervisor section but this bullet was not amended.

summary: I reviewed all four commits against e776cc0 and read the new code closely. Typecheck passes, and so does the full suite: engine 299, workflows 480 with 1 skipped, api 152, web 181. Items 28 and 31 look right, and their tests fail if the fix is broken. Two gaps are worth another round: the run cap is read from the environment of whichever command is running, so a `wf ls` in another shell doesn't see the cap `wf up` was started with; and a queued card whose `repo:` folder is gone is skipped silently. A third point, that a refused card is never retried, is a design choice for a person to confirm.

findings.what: `runSlots` (and `decide`, through it) reads the cap from the environment of the process that calls it, not the daemon's. The README's own example sets it only on the daemon: `WF_MAX_CONCURRENT=4 WF_MAX_RUNS=2 wf up` (README.md:1264). In that setup, `wf ls` in another shell reads a cap of 0, so `heldRuns` returns nothing. A run the daemon is holding then reads plain `waiting`, and `wf decide` on it says `still running: implement` instead of the slot line. A shell with a different `WF_MAX_RUNS` prints a wrong `n of m`. The queue-store tests set `process.env.WF_MAX_RUNS` for the whole test process, so none of them catches this. The record's `slotHeldAt`, which the daemon writes, is never consulted by `wf ls`. Possible fixes: have the daemon record the cap it runs with somewhere `wf ls` reads, or at least word a run with `slotHeldAt` as held. Either needs a test that runs `wf ls` without the variable set.

A queued card whose `repo:` folder has been deleted is never tried and never mentioned on `wf up`. `parseInboxCard` refuses it ('names no directory'), so the catch here builds a listing entry with no `queued`. `queueOrder` and `nextQueued` then leave it out, and `startQueued` never reaches it. `wf up` logs nothing about it, and `wf inbox` shows only the parse error, without the card's place in the queue. The brief says a start refused because 'the repository [is] gone' is named on `wf up`'s line and in `wf inbox`, and README.md:1318 claims the same. Only the workflow-gone case is tested. One fix: read `queued:` without the directory check, so the card stays in the queue order and `startFromInbox` refuses it by name. Add a test that deletes a queued card's `repo:` folder.

For a person to confirm. The brief asked for 'one try per pass'; this code tries a refused card once and then never again until the card's text changes. The catch also takes any error as a lasting refusal, not just the package's exit-2 refusals: a one-off git failure while `start()` sets up the workspace, or a `wf up` briefly run from the wrong folder for a card with no `repo:`, sticks until someone runs `--off` and queues the card again. Putting the missing workflow back does not un-stick it (features.md lists this as left). It also adds a store folder, `$WF_ROOT/queue/`, and a stored refusal that decides later passes, which the brief did not ask for. The reasons are sound: no log spam every 4s, and cards behind a refused one still get their turn. At least consider retrying errors that don't carry exitCode 2 on the next pass.

The three fixes hold, and a full uncached parallel `npx turbo run test --force` and `npm run typecheck` both pass. findings.what: Round totals group every task by `roundIn` of its own step's record (line 2288), and a step outside the loop is always round 1. Take `implement ⇄ review → ship` (a shape the package supports: run.test.ts:1329 has `ship, after the loop`). When the loop goes three rounds, ship is filed after round 3 but counted in round 1's total. So round 1's `ran` includes ship's run time, and round 1's `wall` runs from implement's first filing to ship's end, which is the whole run. `wf decide` prints that as `round 1 ... wall <the run's wall>`, and the run page's tfoot shows the same. A `plan` step before the loop (the shipped `dev-planned`) is also added to round 1, which makes round 1 look slower than later rounds. Only steps in a loop's span (`loopSpan`) should count toward a round's total. Steps outside it count in the run's total alone, or in a row of their own. There is no test with a step outside the loop in `timeline`'s round totals.

`takenBackBy` compares an MCP allow with a deny only when the words are identical, because `ruleOf` returns null for any `mcp__…` name. A settings allow `mcp__fixture__echo` with a deny `mcp__fixture` or `mcp__fixture__*` (from the settings or a step's `disallow:`) stays in `allowed.rules`. For a step not in dontAsk, the page lists `mcp__fixture__echo` under "Allowed without asking", while the same step's MCP tools row strikes `echo` as denied (`denyingRule` does match whole-server denies). It is also missing from `takenBack`. The last round's reply said a deny now takes back every allow whose calls it matches, but that covers Bash only. The fix is to test MCP allows with `denyingRule`'s server / `__*` rule. No test covers a whole-server deny against a single-tool MCP allow.

findings.what: This change adds a new state: an ask for a step that is still running. It is only due on a pass where the engine says `needs-human` (`blockedByHarness`). Case: `wf retry r implement` on a harness-blocked step, then the session starts working again before any tick stops it. §4b records that the operator unblocked sessions by cross-session message on 2026-09-13, and with no `wf up` running the window lasts until the next tick. From then on the ask is not due and `wf ls` shows no note. It is also never spent: `spentAsks` needs `tryOf >= 2`, and the step stays on try 1. If the step later ends failed, stopped or unsigned, or its check refuses, the next pass files try 2 from that old ask at once. The ask branch in `retriesDue` also runs ahead of `retries:`, so nobody is asked again. A task with no `stopRequested` tells this stale ask apart from one whose stop is under way. The tick could honour it by stopping the session anyway, or `wf ls`/`wf decide` could name it; no test covers this.

summary: Reviewed the builder change: the api's three writes, the board's builder and the e2e do what §4 asks, and `npx turbo run test --force` (api 186, web 223, packages unchanged) and `npm run typecheck` are green. Three findings: Save's pasted-schema path writes a schema file before a folder PUT that can be refused and then says nothing was written (with no test of that path); builder.ts holds raw NUL/control bytes that make ripgrep treat it as binary; and Save overwrites or deletes changes made to the folder since the builder opened, with no conflict check.

findings.what: Save writes each pasted schema (PUT …/schemas/:file) before it puts the folder, and the schema PUT only judges the text against the steps already on disk (`judgedWith`, apps/api/src/builder.ts:318). A schema pasted for a new `output:` is named by no step on disk, so any JSON object (`{"type":"object"}`, or a non-strict one) is written with a 200. The folder PUT is then refused by the parser, and the board says "Not saved, and nothing written" (line 187). The file stays in the folder after Discard and is offered in the schema select on the next listing. The same happens when a paste replaces an existing schema and the draft is refused for something unrelated, like a cycle: the file is overwritten and the save refused. Neither the web unit tests nor the e2e exercise the pasted-schema save, so none of this is caught. Judge the pasted schema against the draft before any write (for example, send it with the folder PUT and parse with a `read` override, as `judgedWith` does), or at least say what was written.

The control-character classes in `workflowNameRefusal` (line 172) and `schemaNameRefusal` (line 184) are raw NUL, 0x1F and DEL bytes in the source, not `�-` as the package writes them. Because of the NUL, ripgrep treats builder.ts as binary: a search of `apps/api/src` for `judgedWith` or even `import` returns nothing for this file (checked), and searching the file directly stops with "binary file matches (found \0 byte around offset 11847)". Every later step or person searching the api misses the builder, and a reader sees the class as `[ -]`. Write the escapes.

The PUT writes whatever draft it is sent, with no check that the folder is still what the draft started from, and the builder never re-reads it (`base` is fixed at open, WorkflowBuilder.tsx:63). While the builder is open on `mine`, add `ship.md` by hand, or change `plan.md`'s check in an editor or another tab; then change any key on the board and Save. `writeWorkflow` deletes `ship.md` (shown only afterwards as "removed") and rewrites `plan.md` from the stale draft, silently undoing the edit. That is the read-modify-write lost update CLAUDE.md's one-writer rule warns about. Have the PUT carry what the draft was read from (the listed steps, or a digest of the files) and refuse with a 409 and a reload sentence when the folder no longer reads as it.

summary: The step drag is sound: followers are the steps that wait on the dragged one, the rest stay, moves persist and reset, the uncached test run and the typecheck (replayed from turbo's cache) pass, and both themes read well. The pages were judged from implement's seven screenshots only, because serving the app is denied in this mode and nothing was pressed in a browser. One part of the ask is not done: a card dragged does not take along the cards that wait on it, so I ask for another round on that.

findings.what: The ask was to drag anything, with the right-hand side of the dragged node following and the left staying. That rule is applied to steps only. A card that other runs wait on, joined by the `after` edges the floor draws, moves alone with its own steps. In the e2e's seed, dragging `Lay the diamond top` leaves `One side, shipped`, `The other side, still running` and `The diamond bottom` where they were, and dragging `Called off` leaves `Waits on a called-off run`. The edges stretch across the floor. The hint text admits the asymmetry: `drag to arrange, a step with what follows it`. A card dragged should take the cards that wait on it, directly or through others, by as far, and leave the cards it waits on. It needs a pure function beside `followersOf`, a unit test, and an e2e drag of a card in the seed's diamond that checks what follows and what stays.

`spanOf` claims cells only to the right of the card and below its top. A step dropped left of its card or above it lands on whatever card is there, and nothing moves aside. The step sits on top of that card in this visit and the next, since the move is saved. The comment records this as a choice, and the e2e only checks a drop to the right and down. When a person opens a card that sits between a parent and a child that also wait on each other directly, the parent moves out from under nothing into the opened card's column, and its edge runs backwards. The old code kept that parent where it was.

findings.what: The movedAside path lays the whole group out again even when only an open card can pin it, and the non-strict `placeTogether` then lets `cap` give way, so a card no graph covered lands in a column left of nothing. Example: the triangle b after a, d after a and b (for instance B = api after A = schema, D = web after both), laid out fresh as a (0,0), b (1,0), d (2,0). A person opens b with a 3×1 span. Its graph covers d but not a, so a stays in step 1 and d is movedAside. Then `unput([a])` runs, and `placeTogether([a,d], false)` gets first = col(b)+1−1 = 1 and cap = col(b)−1−0 = 0. Because cap < first it ignores cap and searches columns 1..2. It puts a at (1,1) and d at (2,1). Now a sits directly below b, in b's own column, and the a→b edge runs backwards from a's right side to b's left side. Before this round, a stayed at (0,0) and d went to (2,1), so every edge pointed forward. The same happens for any group where the opened card's parent and child are also joined by a direct edge: the diamond with `d --after a` too, or a chain with a skip. The layering guarantee is the point of the round-one fix, but the new tests only cover the diamond, which has no such edge (its path top→side→bottom leaves room). A `backwards(at, after)` test over the opened triangle would fail today. One fix: when the relayout is infeasible (cap < first) and the down cards were not covered, keep them where they are and place only the loose cards.

All three hold up, and typecheck and the workflows suite pass (429 passed, 1 skipped). One real hole is left: `idRefusal` accepts dots, so `wf rm <id>.json` (or `.cancelled`, `.asks`) takes the no-record path and deletes another run's record, cancellation or asks without any of the refusals. findings.what: `idRefusal` accepts dots, and the files keyed by a run's id are that id plus a suffix, so a dotted id can name another run's files. Take `wf rm r-xyz.json`, which is what `ls ~/.agent-workflows/runs` or tab completion there gives. `runFile('r-xyz.json')` is `runs/r-xyz.json.json`, which does not exist, so `forget` takes the no-record path (runner.ts:1364). `removeKeyed` then removes `path.join(runsDir(), id)` (runner.ts:1483), which is `runs/r-xyz.json`: the real run's record. The line reads `no such run — ... removed runs/r-xyz.json` and exits 0. No check runs first: nothing about in-flight tasks, work due, asks or runs waiting on it. If r-xyz has a session running, that session keeps going in a worktree nothing reads; `wf cancel r-xyz` now says no such run; its worktrees and branches are orphaned; and a child waiting on it reads `(no such run)` for ever. `wf rm r-xyz.cancelled` deletes a cancelled run's `.cancelled`, so the run reads as live and the tick files its next step, which features.md itself names as the danger. `wf rm r-xyz.asks` drops a person's unspent asks. `runId` only mints `[a-z0-9-]` ids, and no id in the machine's store has a dot, so refusing anything else costs nothing. Add a test: `wf rm <id>.json`, `<id>.cancelled` and `<id>.asks` against a live run are refused with exit 2, and its record, cancellation and asks stay.

Minor, and not the reason for another round. The README says a pass halfway through a run that is being forgotten writes nothing back, but `collectArtifacts` runs before any `mayFile` or `rewriteRun` guard and makes its target with `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` (runner.ts:1810). Case: a `--no-worktree` run whose last step has no check stays in `handOffDue` on every pass. If the tick listed the run before `wf rm` and reaches it after, the workspace (the repository itself) is still there, the copies in `runs/<id>/artifacts/<step>/` are gone, and the pass copies the closeout's workspace artifacts back. That recreates `runs/<id>/` with no record. `wf ls` does not show it, and a second `wf rm <id>` sweeps it. Either skip collection when the record no longer exists, or mention it under 'What it leaves'.

findings.what: The approve box's placeholder still reads "Your words (optional): every step after the gate is handed them, under “Approved”." At an ending step's gate nothing follows it, so a person setting the terms of the merge is told their words go nowhere — and they are wrong: `approvedSection` (agent-workflows/src/run.ts:3536) hands an ending step its own approval, "A person approved this step before it was filed … their word is what files it". The panel shown the moment either action is taken is not adapted for `acts`. After a send-back at an ending's gate it reads "ship try 2 asked — the next tick files it", naming `ship` for a try that was filed for `review` (`askedSaid` says only "try N", and the `<strong>` above it is `step`). An ending step's `gate` facts row reads "holds once it has signed off" for the whole of the run before its gate holds, and again after a send-back — visible under `ship` in decide-sent-back-light/dark.png. Pre-existing, but it is on the screen this change is about.

`standingsOf` puts `git` on `GET /api/runs`, which the Factory and Runs poll every five seconds and which ran none before (the new test proves it). Each finished, succeeded, isolate run whose folder does not merge costs 2-3 `execFileSync` spawns per result branch — `isShipped`'s two `merge-base --is-ancestor`, or one plus `rev-parse` and `rev-list` — in a sequential loop over every run (app.ts:1772), so the api's single event loop is blocked for the sum: 580 ms at 68 branches on the author's own store (RESPONSE.md), growing with the store, with every other request and every SSE session stream waiting behind it. Nothing caps or caches it. Disclosed rather than missed, and the remedies are a design call for a person: one `git for-each-ref --merged`/`--contains` per repository instead of two calls per branch, or an answer cached against the branch tip.

summary: Reviewed the whole change against §8 and ran the suite: `npm run typecheck` clean and `npx turbo run test --force` green at the claimed counts (agent-workflows 575/574+1 skipped, api 200, web 243, engine 326). findings.what: Nothing keeps two runs' ending steps out of the same checkout. `validate` refuses a second ending inside one workflow, but `workspaceFor` hands `run.repo` to any approved ending, and `tick` advances every run in one pass: approve two finished `dev` runs (the board's `to decide` list invites exactly that) and the next pass files both `ship` tasks with `cwd` = the repository, and the engine runs both at once (pool cap 2 by default). Both sessions read `git status --porcelain` as clean, both run `git merge --no-ff --no-commit`, and the loser's `git merge --abort` (step 5 of its own prose) throws away the winner's staged trial merge while the winner's `npm test` is running against it — two opus sessions wasted and the person's checkout rewritten under them. The only thing standing in the way is ship.md's prose, and the house rule is that the machinery refuses the alternative. A level-triggered refusal to file an ending while another run has one unsettled in the same repo (the store's other runs are already read for `forgetRefusal`) is the shape; there is no test for two runs at all.

The ending step gets the standard artifacts contract, whose second bullet is false for it and invites damage: "Or leave it in this workspace, and name it in `artifacts` by its path from the workspace root … the run copies each such file into that directory … A file left in the workspace is committed with the rest too." For a `workspace: main` step "this workspace" is the person's checkout, and `handOffDue` (run.ts:1132) now excludes the step, so `collectArtifacts` (runner.ts:1546) never runs and nothing is committed. A ship session that writes `merge-log.md` beside its closeout, as its brief tells it to, leaves an untracked file in the person's checkout for ever — and the next run's ship step then reads `git status --porcelain` as non-empty and signs off blocked at step 1 of its prose. It also contradicts ship.md's own "leave the checkout as you found it". Give a main-workspace step a contract with only the absolute-path bullet.

The send-back refusal at an ending's gate names the wrong step's gate and a command that is itself refused. On the shipped `dev` folders, `wf retry <run> review` (no --message) at ship's gate reaches the `sendsBack` branch added at run.ts:1317 and prints "review is awaiting approval: a try of it sends it back from its gate … — or approve it: wf approve <run> review." review is not awaiting approval (`wf ls` shows it `unverified · done`, ship `awaiting approval`), and `wf approve <run> review` is refused by `approvalRefusal` with "review has no gate … <run> is gated at ship." It should say ship is the step at its gate and name `wf approve <run> ship`. The test at test/run.test.ts:3320 does not catch it: `/^review is awaiting approval|--message/` is an alternation, so it passes whatever the sentence says.

`decision` does not apply `unheld`, so `wf decide` and the board contradict `wf ls` in the window the round-3 fix was meant to close. Between `wf retry <run> review --message "…"` and the pass that files it, `standing` still reads ship as `awaiting approval`: `wf decide` prints "AWAITING APPROVAL, waiting on you: ship — your approval is what runs it" and `gateLines` prints `wf approve <run> ship`, while `wf ls` (which does apply `unheld`) shows ship `waiting` with nothing to decide, and `wf approve <run> ship` is refused with "try 2 of review is asked for … approving now would take the result that ask objects to." The api's run page reads `decision` and `gateLines` too, so its Approve button is live in the same window. `decision` should take the same `unheld` adjustment `assess` and `listing` take.

`wf retry <run> ship` at the ending's gate — the step `wf ls` names on the line above the send-back — falls through to the default "ship is awaiting approval, and there is nothing to try again." Before this change every `awaiting approval` step had modes (a step with no followers hit the first `sendsBack` clause), so this state is new and lands on a message that names no fix: it should point at `wf approve <run> ship` and `wf retry <run> <the work> --message`, as `sendBackTo` already computes.

`wf round <run> review` at an ending's gate is refused with "…its loop is over and there is nothing to go round again. What waits on it has been filed: wf ls <run>." Nothing has been filed — ship is unfiled and waiting for the person's approval, which is the whole state they are standing in. `roundAsk`'s gate check at run.ts:1903 only looks inside `loopSpan`, so the ending's gate is invisible to it; the sentence should say the run is at its ending's gate and name `wf approve` / the send-back.

The board now tells a person to merge by hand a branch whose run has an ending step waiting to merge it. `commandsOf` offers `ship it  git merge --no-ff <branch>` and `drop it  git branch -D …` for any awaiting decision with branches, and a `dev` run parked at ship's gate is one — while `wf decide` deliberately suppresses both for a folder that merges (cli.ts:889, `!merges(steps)`). Outside your package, so the fix is one line for the board run (pass `merges(steps)` the way the CLI does); at minimum it belongs in features.md's "What it leaves", which does not name it.

summary: Reviewed the inbox's api routes, the /inbox page, the e2e and the docs against the brief. The api and web suites and typecheck pass (typecheck replayed from turbo's cache). findings.what: `POST /api/inbox` saves `repo` exactly as sent, but `wf inbox add --repo` cleans the path first (`path.resolve`, cli.ts:451). Someone who types `/home/me/code/app/` with a trailing slash in the Repository box gets a card with `repo: /home/me/code/app/`. `startFromInbox` then records `run.repo` with the slash, and the board matches runs by exact string (StartRun.tsx:121). So that card's start form says 'No run on this repository to wait on', and the Workflows page never offers the new run as one to wait on. The same function already uses `path.resolve(about)` to decide whether to write the workflow by name (line 113) but saves the raw value. Fix: save `path.resolve(about)` when `about` is absolute; leave a relative path as sent so the package still refuses it. Add a test that files a path with a trailing slash and asserts the card's `repo:` has none.

When a card's run is written but its file cannot be removed, the api answers 201 with `removed: false` and `why`. `StartRun` shows `why` (`data-kept`), but its `onSuccess` also refetches the inbox (StartRun.tsx:41). The refetched entry has `startedAs = [id]`, so `startable` is false and `{starting && startable && <StartCard/>}` unmounts the form and the message within milliseconds. The person sees only the generic 'Started as …, and still here because its removal failed' line, never the error itself (e.g. EACCES). features.md says 'A card that stayed says why, and the page stays', which does not hold. Nothing tests this case: no api test reaches `removed: false`, and the web and e2e tests only parse the answer. Fix: keep the start form's result mounted after a start that did not remove the card (or show `why` on the card), and add a test that covers it.

summary: Reviewed the two commits against d611627: api `tries`/`filed`/artifacts route and the inspector's Rounds, Output closeouts, spec rows and inline images. The engine files the task without a mode, then its claude runner spawns with `--permission-mode auto` (packages/agent-engine/src/runner.ts:626), and codex runs `workspace-write`, or `read-only` when `tools` has none of Bash/Write/Edit (runner-detached.ts:359-363). The workflow sets no `model`, and a person runs `wf retry <run> <step> --model sonnet`. The runner files the try with `model: r.model ?? step.model` (agent-workflows runner.ts:817), so `filed.model` is `sonnet` and `ranWith` marks it `sonnet · default`. Not a correctness bug, and it is what the brief prescribed, but a person should know. `detail` now calls `e.view` once per distinct task of every try, and each call runs a fresh harness observation: a `claude agents` call plus a scan of detached runs (agent-engine facade.ts:315), one after another. findings.what: Nothing tests the `RouterProvider` that `__root.tsx:37` adds. Remove it and Enter on a sidebar place (Runs, say) reloads the whole page again, with every check still green, because the e2e only clicks links. Why: pressing Enter on a focused `<a>` makes the browser fire a click, and React Aria does not stop it. `usePress`'s onClick ignores a keyboard press (usePress.mjs:290), and `handleLinkClick` does nothing without a provider (openLink.mjs:147), so the browser follows the link. CLAUDE.md now asks for a check by hand instead. A check that fails without the provider: set a marker on `window`, focus a place's link, press Enter, wait for the URL, then assert the marker is still there and `history.length` grew by one.

This trap, the comment at `apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:35` and features.md:2702 all say Enter makes a click that 'never reaches the router's `onClick`'. That is wrong. The router's `onClick`, and `picked` merged into it, does run on Enter, but on keyup through `triggerSyntheticClick` (usePress.mjs:311). By then the browser's own click from keydown has already started a full page load. With the provider in place, Enter now navigates twice: once through React Aria's `router.open` on keydown, then through TanStack's `onClick` on keyup. The second goes to the same URL, so TanStack calls `router.load()` again (router-core router.js:408) and the loaders run twice. Someone who trusts the current wording could conclude that `onClick={picked}` never runs on Enter and move it, or look for the bug in the wrong place. Say what actually happens: the browser's click from keydown is not prevented, and the router's handler only runs on keyup.

`SidebarMenu` and `SidebarMenuItem` changed from `ul`/`li` to `div`/`div`. A screen reader no longer announces the main nav as a list of five places. features.md:2734 puts this under 'what the base does not offer', but React Aria plays no part in it: the aria-nova registry just ships `div`s. Putting back `ul`/`li` (and the `React.ComponentProps` types) is a two-line local edit, like `showCloseButton={false}`, not a workaround of the base. Either restore the list and note it as a local edit, or move this out of the base's limits and call it the registry's markup, kept on purpose.

summary: Round 2 review of `wf start --after`. Both round-1 fixes hold: the gate now says `shipped` only when the parent's own `decision` does, and features.md now says the api builds its responses field by field. Checks pass: agent-workflows 313 passed with 1 skipped, api 89 passed, typecheck clean. Two gaps remain. `wf start` silently drops `--after=<id>` or a misspelt flag, so the run starts at once. A child with two parents never starts if one parent's branch is deleted after its merge while the other parent is still under review, and the README says this cannot happen in practice.

findings.what: `afterOf` only matches the bare `--after` token, and `wf start` refuses no argument it does not know. So `wf start b.md --after=a-1x2y` (or a typo, `--afer a-1x2y`) writes a run with no `after`. The next tick files its roots straight away, on a base without a-1x2y's work: silently, the one thing the flag exists to prevent, and the sessions are spent. The sibling verbs refuse this: `decideHow` refuses any flag it does not take, and `retryHow` reads `--message=` and refuses the rest. No test makes `wf start` refuse an `=`-joined or misspelt `--after`.

`parentOf` returns `shipped: false` as soon as any result branch is `gone`, even when that branch's work is on the base. In the diamond, D is gated until the slower of B and C ships. If B is merged and `git worktree remove` + `git branch -d`'d while C is still in review, then after C ships D still reads `waiting on B (wf/B/implement gone)` for ever. B's work is on main, and the only way out is to cancel D and start it again without `--after B`. The request's rule was that a parent whose branch 'no longer exists and is not on the base' reads as not shipped, which implies one that is gone but on the base reads as shipped. features.md:633 gives the reason for not recording the tip as 'the request said shipped is read from git'. That does not hold: `merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> <base>` is still git's answer, and the tip would be the parent's own fact, written by the parent's own tick. No test covers a two-parent child where one parent's branch is deleted before the other parent ships.

'With `wf up` running, the child starts on the pass after the merge, well before anyone gets round to deleting the branch' is false for any child with two or more parents, the diamond's D included. Such a child does not start on the pass after one parent's merge. It waits for the last parent, which can take hours of review, and that is when a person cleans up the first parent's branch. A reader who trusts the sentence deletes merged branches as usual and strands D. It needs correcting whether or not the behaviour changes.

summary: I reviewed S1 (`transcript` on both runners, `Engine.transcript`, README, open issues) against 9caf10d. Tests and typecheck pass: the engine package run directly gave 229 passing, 0 failing and 3 skipped (the live tests), and every requested refusal test is there. Two things need a short second round. The engine checks every cursor against the file reader's own format, so a `PromiseRunner` that makes its own cursors is refused on its second read. And `transcript` fails whenever `claude agents` fails, even for a finished task whose session id is already in the journal, where `logs` still works. I could not check the Codex reader against real rollouts: reading `~/.codex/sessions` was denied, so its record shapes are only as good as the implementer's measurement.

findings.what: `Engine.transcript` refuses any `after` that does not match `readTranscript`'s `<offset>.<16 hex>` format, for every harness. But `PromiseRunner.transcript` is documented to take "a cursor this method returned", so a custom runner owns its cursor. Say one returns `{ events, cursor: 'page-2' }` or `'42'`: the next `engine.transcript(id, 'page-2')` is rejected with exitCode 2 ("`page-2` is not a cursor a transcript read gave"), and a board can never get past that harness's first read. Such a runner is also later handed the engine's own START cursor (`0.e3b0c442…`), which it never returned. The test at test/transcript.test.ts:443 hides this by giving its PromiseRunner a cursor already in the file format (`'7.0123456789abcdef'`). Either leave the format check to the built-in file reader (still mapped to exitCode 2) and pass a PromiseRunner's cursor through untouched, or state and enforce the format in the `PromiseRunner` contract. Add a test with a cursor in a runner's own format.

`transcript` calls the task's harness's `observe` directly, with no fallback. `logs` goes through `composite`, which turns a failed `observe` into an empty map (runner-composite.ts:35-38) and so falls back to the journal's `last.nativeId`. Concretely: take a finished `claude` task whose session id is in the journal. If `claude agents --all --json` fails or prints something that is not JSON (the contention CLAUDE.md records for the api tests), `engine.logs(id)` still reads the transcript but `engine.transcript(id)` rejects, even though the file read never needed the registry. summary: The routes, the fold, the session page, the Activity tab and the tests that were asked for are all there. I reran the new tests without turbo's cache: 8 api transcript tests and 18 web tests pass, and the apps/web typecheck passes. Root `npm test` and typecheck came from turbo's cache, for the same inputs. No Claude Code web link was added, and the registry row the engine parses has no URL field. Five findings: transcript.ts contains a NUL byte, so git shows the file as binary; parallel calls read "No result" while they run; one failed poll on the stream ends live following for good, with no test; the session screenshots never show the fold line; and each open stream runs `claude agents` twice a second.

findings.what: `keyOf` joins `kind` and `id` with a literal NUL byte in the source (cat -v shows `${event.kind}^@${event.id}`). Because of that byte, git treats the whole file as binary: `git diff --numstat c6ce655` gives `-	-` and `git diff` prints `Bin 0 -> 11342 bytes`. So the person who merges, and any PR view, sees none of the fold's ~250 lines. Later edits or a conflicting merge of this file also get no line diff and no textual 3-way merge. Write the escape `'�'` instead, or use a printable separator: `kind` is a closed set with no ':', so `${kind}:${id}` is unambiguous.

While live, a call without a result counts as running only if it is the fold's last call (`last && inner === lastCall`; `stateOf` at :79). Claude Code writes parallel calls as consecutive tool_use lines, and their results come after all of them. So while a batch runs (say three Bash calls from one message), every call but the last shows 'No result' with a grey circle in the opened fold. That looks like a dropped call until its result lands. In a fold that is last while the session is live, every call without a result is still running, so pass `running = live && last` to each call. Add a test: a live fold with two pending calls shows both as `running`.

One failed read on the stream sends `unreadable` and returns. The client (`useStepTranscript.ts:56`) then closes the EventSource for good. Any rejection triggers this: `e.view` failing on a journal read (EMFILE under load, say) or `e.transcript` failing to open the file for a moment. The page then drops 'following live' and says the conversation 'could not be read any further' while the session keeps running, until someone reloads. The rest of the design is level-triggered, and the next second's read would most likely succeed. Nothing tests this branch, and nothing tests the /transcript route's 502 either, although /log has a 502 test. Simplest fix: close the stream without `settled`, so the EventSource reconnects from Last-Event-ID on its own. Or keep polling. Add a test that makes one read fail and checks that following resumes.

The session page is a full-height scroller that opens at its end, so `fullPage` (visit.ts:38) captures only the last 800 px. Neither session-light.png nor session-dark.png shows the prompt bubble, the opened thought, or the fold line 'Ran 3 commands, searched code, read 3 files · 1 failed'. That line is the main thing the brief asked for, and nobody has seen it in either theme. The Activity tab in run-*.png also shows only the tail (Edit, a system line, the closeout). The DOM assertions pass, but the screenshots do not show what they checked. Scroll the conversation to the top at the end of the page's `expect`, or photograph the fold, before the shot.

Every read calls `e.view` only to learn `settled`. That call checks every harness: `claude agents --all --json`, plus the Claude runner's pass over the closeout and usage of every idle `ae/` session. Then `e.transcript` runs `claude agents` again for an attempt still in flight. So each open session page or Activity tab on a running Claude step spawns the registry twice a second, plus the idle-session reads. packages/agent-engine/docs/open-issues.md expects one call per poll (~300 ms) and says nobody has measured this. `settled` is also in the journal: `engine.feed`, with a cursor the stream holds after one initial view, reports it without querying any harness. findings.what: `retriesDue` accepts an ask with no message for a step at its gate. `retryable` gives such a step `nudge`/`fresh` through `sendsBack`, but the rule that a send-back needs words lives only in `retryRefusal`, which only the CLI calls. The tick never checks it. A concrete path through the CLI, the one `retriesDue`'s own doc describes: a gated `plan` is running and its harness blocks it, so a person types `wf retry r plan` with no words, which is allowed for a harness-blocked step. The session works again, signs off `done` and settles before a tick stops it. On the next pass `plan` reads `awaiting approval`, `sendsBack` is true, and the wordless `retry-plan-2` is due. The tick files try 2 at once: the session is continued with `status: 'awaiting approval'`, and its brief says a person "sent it back rather than let it go on: what they want changed is below", with nothing below. Nobody read the plan or approved it, `wf ls` never said `approve plan`, and a try is spent. Without the gate the same ask is not due, because an `unverified` step has no modes. A hand-written `{"mode":"nudge"}` file at the gate does the same thing, although the README says hand-written asks are held to the verb's word. Fix: when `sendsBack` holds, count only an ask with `message !== undefined` as due. Add a test where a wordless ask for try n+1 on a step at its gate is not due across passes, and the step stays `awaiting approval`, waiting on you.

The `already approved` refusal assumes nothing has been filed yet. Say `plan` is approved and `implement` and `review` have already run, or a one-step gated run is approved and merged. `wf approve r plan` then says "what waits on it is filed on the next tick, once. To send it back instead, before that tick: wf retry r plan --message …". Both claims are false: nothing is due, and that `wf retry` is refused (`plan signed off done … what waits on it has been filed`). The error sends the person to a command that refuses them. Say the send-back part only while `retryable(...).sendsBack` holds; otherwise say the step has handed on.

summary: Reviewed `wf rm` against the brief: the pure judgement in run.ts, `forget` and the write-back guard in runner.ts, the CLI, and the README and features.md. It covers the brief and the tests are real (package suite 424 tests, 423 passing and 1 skipped; typecheck clean). Three gaps remain, all ways to lose work or leave a run's session running with nothing watching it: forgetting a run cancelled while a pass is still filing its step, a hand-off commit that git refuses, and a worktree whose HEAD is not on a branch.

findings.what: On a cancelled run, `forgetRefusal` never judges a ready step, and `forget` never looks for a step a pass has filed but not yet written down (runner.ts:1324-1326 looks for checks, tries and rounds only). Simplest case: `wf start`, then while the first pass is cutting implement's worktree (`npm ci` can take a minute) the person types `wf cancel` then `wf rm`. `cancel` sees nothing running and marks the run. `wf rm` sees a cancelled run with nothing running, removes the worktree and the record. The pass then calls `e.file` with a working directory that is gone (runner.ts:1186), and `rewriteRun` quietly writes nothing. The session is now on the engine's board, and no pass will ever stop it: every pass stops a cancelled run's work, but only a run it can find a record for. `npm ci` can also create `worktrees/<id>/<step>/node_modules` again, the disk `wf rm` was meant to free. The brief says a ready step counts because a pass may be filing it at that moment, and a step being filed has not settled. features.md mentions the gap, but says only that nothing reads the task, not that nothing stops it. Possible fix: on a cancelled run, look up the task id each would-be-ready step would get (`stepTaskId(run, name, tryOf(run, name))`) and count it as running if the engine has it, as the existing check/try/round lookups do. And in `advance`, just before each `e.file`, re-check that the record still exists and the run is not cancelled. Add a store test that holds a pass between cutting the worktree and filing while `cancel` and `forget` run.

If the hand-off commit fails, `handOff` hides why: a failing pre-commit hook (husky/lint-staged on a failed step's broken code) or `commit.gpgsign=true` with no agent is enough. `git worktree remove` then refuses the dirty tree, so the work is safe, but the run's line only passes on git's first stderr line: `fatal: '<wt>' contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it`. The only advice the person gets is the one command that deletes the failed step's uncommitted work. The line never says the commit was tried and refused, or why, and `wf rm` again repeats the same thing. It should say the hand-off could not commit (with the commit's own error) and give a safe next step, such as committing in the worktree yourself. Or the forget hand-off could commit with `--no-verify -c commit.gpgsign=false`, since its only job is to keep the work. No store test has a hand-off commit that fails.

A worktree whose HEAD is detached (git lists it with no `branch`) is handed off and removed like any other. The commit is made on the detached HEAD, and `git worktree remove` then leaves it, plus any commits the session made there, on no branch and unreachable. The line still says `committed what <step> left uncommitted as abc1234` (without `on <branch>`), which reads as if the work was kept. How a step ends up there: its session ran `git rebase`, `git bisect` or `git checkout <sha>` and was stopped or hit its deadline, exactly the failed or stopped work the brief says lives only in the worktree. Such a worktree should hold the run and be named, as a locked one is, unless its HEAD is already on a branch.

findings.what: `postLine`'s 5 s timeout rejects even after `written` is true. By then the line is in the socket buffer, and Claude Code reads it once its event loop gets to the connection. So when a session's process is stalled for more than 5 s, the session still gets the words, but `Engine.say` says `was not given the words (... took nothing within 5000 ms). Nothing was journalled.` That is delivery with no trace, the failure `say` exists to prevent, and a person who says it again sends it twice with one entry on the record. Fix: once `written`, a timeout while waiting for the inbox to close should resolve (the words were handed over), or reject with a message that says they may have arrived. No test covers this: add an inbox that reads the line and never closes.

The check that refuses a socket owned by another uid is only ever tested allowing. The one `uid` parameter feeds both the registration check and the socket check, so a test passing another uid (say.test.ts) is stopped by the registration check first and never reaches this line. CLAUDE.md requires every new refusal to be made to refuse. Fix: give the socket check its own uid parameter, or pull the checks on the socket's stat into a pure function a test can hand another uid, and test it refusing.

`say` accepts a session listed `blocked`, and README.md:715 and this comment state as fact that it reads the words once it moves again. The probe measured only a busy session and an idle one. A `--bg` session blocked on a permission prompt that nobody attaches to may never move. B8's board then continues it as a new attempt that never gets the words, while the journal says they were said to the old one. Either measure the blocked case live, or add it to open-issues.md as half-verified beside issue 12.

The transcript check passes on any event whose `text` contains the file name, including the model's own text such as 'Writing SAID-….txt'. So it can pass even if the new attachment reader (runner.ts, `queued_command` with a `peer` origin) is broken. Restrict it to `e.kind === 'system'` with the exact words. Separately, `engine.say` at line 254 is outside `settleThenCheck`'s try/finally, so a rejection there leaves both `--bg` sessions running and registered. Also, open-issues.md records no run of this test, yet runner.ts:913 cites `test/live.test.ts` as the measurement; the measurement was the hand probe (artifacts/implement/say-probe.md). Run it with AE_LIVE=1 and record the result, or cite the probe instead.

summary: I reviewed the inbox change against 8f792b1. findings.what: `inboxNameOf` only treats a path as a card when it ends in `.md`, but `wf inbox` and `wf inbox rm` show and take names without `.md`. So `wf start ~/.agent-workflows/inbox/cache-the-views-k2q9 --workflows dev` (the name copied from the list) returns null. No such file exists, so cli.ts takes the path text itself as the brief: `start()` writes and runs a run whose brief is `/home/me/.agent-workflows/inbox/cache-the-views-k2q9`, pays for it, and leaves the card in the inbox. The request says `wf start <path under the inbox>` goes through the start function. Suggested fix: send any path directly in the inbox, with or without `.md`, to `startFromInbox`, so a missing card gets the existing refusal that names the cards there are. Add a test for the path without `.md`. The existing test that asserts `<inbox>/notes.txt` gives null would need to change too.

`wf inbox add <file>` copies the file's own `workflow:` word for word, while cli.ts:445 makes only a `--workflow` flag path absolute. A relative path in the file meant a folder relative to where that file was, as a plan card's path is read from its plan folder. Once the card is in the inbox, `startFromInbox` reads it from the inbox folder instead. Example: a card in `<repo>/plans/` with `workflow: ../workflows/dev` means `<repo>/workflows/dev`. Filed and started, it means `~/.agent-workflows/workflows/dev`, the home workflow store. If a workflow named `dev` exists there, the run silently uses it instead of the repository's. Otherwise the start is refused with a path the person never wrote. Suggested fix: make a path-like `workflow:` from the file absolute against the file's folder when filing, the same way the flag is. Add a test.

The `after:` refusal builds its advice from `file`. When `wf inbox add ./ideas/d.md` hits it, `file` is the path that was given, so the message says `wf start <inbox>/./ideas/d.md --after <runId>`: a command that names no card. What the person needs to do is delete the line, file the idea, then give `--after` when starting the filed card. The test at inbox-store.test.ts:153 only checks the start of the message, so this passes.

findings.what: A try the checkout holds is filtered out of `retry`, so the `status.set(r.step, 'running')` on the next line never runs and the ending keeps a status that stops followers — `assess` then calls the whole run `failed`. Take the case the change's own test builds (ship.test.ts, "a try of an ending step waits for the checkout…"): ship signed off blocked, the person typed `wf retry <run> ship --message "…"`, another run's ship has the checkout. `wf decide <run>` no longer prints "still running: ship" — `decision` never reaches its running branch, so the ended screen prints "BLOCKED, waiting on you: ship" and then offers "ship: blocked. Continue its session, told what happened:  wf retry <run> ship" (retryLines) plus the same command again under ship's `needs` (answerLines) — a command `retryRefusal` refuses with "try 2 of ship is already asked for". At the same moment `wf ls` of that run lists nobody in `waitingOnYou` and says "try 2 asked (--nudge) — waiting on the checkout": the two screens disagree about whether anything waits on the person. `advance` also returns `status: 'failed'` and `inFlight: false` (slotNeed counts `retry`), so a run merely queued behind another's ending stops counting against the cap on runs in flight and a queued run is admitted in its place. Nothing records that the board cannot see the hold, though the same document records the `commandsOf` gap it does leave. `checkoutHold` is async and lives in runner.ts; apps/api/src/app.ts:722 calls `listing(...)` with no `checkout` and app.ts:730/1319 call `assess`/`decision` without one, so on the Factory an approved ending held behind another run's ship draws the plain word `waiting` — indistinguishable from an approved ending the next tick will file — and a held try draws a run still running with a try due. The careful choice of `waiting on the checkout (…)` over `waiting for …`, made so `stepState` draws it as a step with nothing filed, reaches no board today. A person watching the board sees a run stop for minutes with no word for why; `wf ls` is the only place that says it.

findings.what: `parentOf` counts a parent as shipped only if every result branch has commits past the parent's `baseRef` (`!isAncestor(b, baseRef)`). That extra condition is not in `wf decide`'s check. Take a parent that has finished (succeeded, every step verified) but whose result branch has no commits past its base, for example a brief that was already done or a step that found nothing to change. Its `wf decide` prints `shipped — wf/p/implement is already on main`, because `decision` calls `isShipped` on a finished run. Meanwhile its child is stuck. `wf ls` shows a plain `waiting on p`, with no bracketed reason and no `→ waiting on you` line. `wf decide <child>` says `nothing of c is filed until p is on main; nothing to decide yet`. `wf start --after p` is accepted instead of refused. Nothing tells the person the child will never start or how to get out. The condition was added so a child would not start the moment the parent's first step was filed, which only matters while the parent is still running. One fix: apply it only to a parent that has not finished. Another: treat a finished parent with no new work as never shipping, with a reason in brackets, an entry in `waitAdvice`, and a refusal in `afterRefusal`. Either way, add a store test where the parent's step signs off with no commit.

It says "`/api/runs` already carries `after`, since the record passes through." That is false. `summarize` (apps/api/src/app.ts:464-486) and `detail` (app.ts:508-534) build the response field by field, and neither includes `after`. summary: Nearly all of what was asked is built. The loader skips the README and reads its description, the three workflows exist (ui matches the package's copy file for file), both api routes and their refusals are tested, and the Workflows page, sidebar item and workflow links work; I checked the page in both themes in implement's screenshots. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass from the root, though turbo replayed cached results rather than rerunning; I did not run build or e2e. One finding is worth another round: the board's first write, POST /api/runs, can be triggered from another website or another machine. The other two can wait.

findings.what: POST /api/runs accepts a request from any other website. `c.req.json()` parses the body whatever its content-type, and nothing checks `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site`. So any page the person visits can run `fetch('http://localhost:8787/api/runs', {method: 'POST', body: '{"workflow":"dev","brief":"…"}'})`. That body is sent as text/plain, so the browser does not ask the server first, and the api answers 201 and writes a run record with the attacker's brief. The same works through vite's `/api` proxy on :5173. On top of that, `apps/api/src/main.ts:14` calls `serve` with no hostname, so the api listens on every network interface and anyone on the network can POST directly. Once `wf up` is running, it files that run and a Claude session (`--permission-mode auto`) acts on the attacker's text in the person's repository. GETs were already exposed, but this is the first write. Fix: answer 415 unless the content-type is `application/json`, refuse a cross-site `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site`, and bind to 127.0.0.1. Add a test that sends a text/plain POST and a cross-site POST, expects both refused, and checks no record is written.

`foldersIn` lists every directory, hidden ones included. If a person keeps `~/.agent-workflows/workflows/` in git (a natural thing for personal workflows), `.git` shows up as a red card: `.git has no .md steps in it`. An editor folder such as `.vscode` under `<repo>/workflows/` does the same, and the 404 message lists them among the workflows there are. Skip names that start with `.`, and add a test with a hidden folder in the fixture.

No automated test covers the web half of starting a run. The e2e deliberately never presses Start, and neither `startRun` nor `StartRun` (`apps/web/src/routes/workflows.tsx:99`) has a unit or component test. If `startRun` stopped reading `body.error` from a 422, or lost the returned id, the page would show `POST /api/runs answered 422 Unprocessable Entity` or no link, and every check would still pass. implement's screenshots start-started and start-refused show it working once, by hand. A small test of `startRun` with a stubbed `fetch` (201 gives `{ id }`; 422, 404 and 409 reject with the api's message word for word; a non-JSON 500 gives the status line) would cover it.

summary: I reviewed the change against 35920da. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both passed, and I read implement's e2e photographs in both themes. The api is sound: its `after`, `waiting`, `moving` and decision fields are held to the package's own `list` and `decide` by tests, the refusals are tested at shipped defaults, and the default Factory floor draws the diamond as a diamond. findings.what: The parents-left-of-children layering only holds for a fresh layout. When a graph covers some cards of a joined group but not others, `joined` (line 193) only collects the unplaced ones, so the layering is worked out over a partial group. And `first` only keeps a card right of its placed parents, never left of its placed children. The e2e hits this, and its own photograph shows it (implement/factory-light.png). After Reset layout, FAKE's graph covers top, shipped and bottom but not running, so those three are re-placed as a straight row (top col0, shipped col1, bottom col2). Opening the neighbour's graph then moves running, which is placed alone with first = top's column + 1 and lands in col 3, right of bottom, which waits on it. The running→bottom edge then runs backwards under the cards. The same happens with a person's saved positions, which step 2 restores one card at a time. Fix: cap a lone card's column below its placed children, or re-place the whole joined group once any member moves. Add a `placeRuns` test that starts from `onFloor` with only one diamond card displaced; the current tests only lay out from empty.

On a card whose root says `waiting on <run>`, the chip gets `max-w-full` and the step name is the part that shrinks. The bottom card in factory-diamond-light.png and factory-diamond-dark.png shows the step as "i…" beside `waiting on the-other-side-runs-e2e6`. A longer id, or a `(cancelled)` or `(<branch> gone)` suffix, leaves no name at all. The card already carries the full word on its own `data-waiting` line, so the name should keep its width (`shrink-0`) and the chip should truncate instead.

The Runs row decides "waiting on you" from `run.waitingOnYou` alone. A run waiting on a cancelled, missing or gone parent has `waitingOnYou: []` and `waiting.onYou: true`, so its row never says it waits on you. runs-light.png shows 'Waits on a called-off run' with no amber line, while the Factory counts it among "3 waiting on you". The row should use `waitsOnYou(run)`, which the Factory already uses, so the two pages agree.

`runWord` calls any run that is not in flight and not cancelled "finished". The picker therefore labels 'Waits on a called-off run' as `finished` (start-refused-light.png), though it has never filed a step and never will without a person. `afterRefusal` accepts it as a parent: it is not cancelled and has no result branch to be gone. So a person who trusts the label starts a child that waits behind a run blocked for ever. It should say `waiting on you` for a run where `waitsOnYou(run)` is true, or show `waiting.word`.

`neverShips` is copied from run.ts, where it is not exported, and `onYou`, which drives `moving` and the Factory's in-flight split, rests on the copy. The brief said to stop and say so rather than re-derive what the package does not export. If the package gains a reason a parent never ships, `waitAdvice` will say "yours to resolve" while the api still reports the run as moving, in flight on the Factory. The api test copies the same rule, so it would not catch that. At least name the missing export in the closeout so a person can export `neverShips` from the package.

The same after a raise: `wf retry --budget 10` after $4.25 spent gives the new session $10, so the step can reach $14.25. The README's table warns of a one-try overrun only on `claude`. In the very pass where `assess` returns `round: [review]` it also returns `toDecide: {kind:'approve', step:'ship'}` and `ship: awaiting approval`, so `wf ls` and the board say `→ to decide: Ship it: trial merge … — wf approve <run> ship` at the moment the reviewer asked for the work to be changed; the window lasts until the next tick files the round, and for ever if no `wf up` is running. `approvalRefusal`'s new guard (line 342) only looks for a pending RetryAsk on a step in `after`, and a round asked by `again: true` writes no ask, so the approval is accepted, is written against ship's try 1, and nothing ever spends it (`spentApprovals` needs `try < tryOf`, and the round resets review, not ship). When the extra round finishes, the tick files ship and the merge runs on work whose final review the person never saw. Reachable in every shipped `dev*` folder, since ship waits on the looping review step.

For a run started `--no-worktree` (`isolate: false`), every step's branch is the base branch, so `resultSteps(...).map(branch)` is `['main']` and the ending step's brief reads "The work of review is not in this directory: it is on main, cut from `<sha>`" — false, the work is in that directory — and hands it `git log --oneline main..main` and `git diff main...main`, which print nothing. A session following the shipped `ship.md` then runs `git merge --no-ff --no-commit main` on main (a no-op, exit 0), runs the folder's whole check, has `git commit --no-edit` fail with nothing to commit, and `git merge --abort` fail with no merge in progress, so the ending signs off `blocked` after paying for a full suite run. Nothing refuses the combination, and decide.test.ts builds exactly such a run (`isolate: false` with a `workspace: main` ending) to test the screen, so the path is live and untested for the brief.

`endingSteps` is any terminal gated step, so `wf start --workflows workflows/ui --gate review` makes review an "ending": at its gate the run says `→ to decide: Review the change in this workspace as a second engineer would. — wf approve …` (the step's own instructions, offered as what happens next), and once approved `toDecide` is undefined while `ending.length` is 1, so `wf decide` prints neither the to-decide block nor `ship it`/`drop it`. The branch holding all of that run's work is left with no command anywhere on the screen. §8 justified dropping the git commands for a research ending because that branch "holds nothing"; here it holds everything, and the run has no `workspace: main` step that would merge it.

findings.what: A step that signed off blocked and is over its budget can't be answered from the board. The package's own offer for this case is `wf retry <run> <step> --budget <amount> --message "<answer>"` (`answerLines`), and `retryLines` says `--recheck … needs no --budget` for a refused check. The run page's banner explains every step waiting on you with a fixed list of reasons: "signed off blocked, unsigned, refused by its check, or out of rounds". findings.what: `sendsBack` stays open while the step is approved and none of its dependents is filed. A gated step with no dependents never has one filed, so once approved it can be sent back for ever. Example: gate.test.ts's one-step parent, `start({ gates: ['implement'] })`. After `wf approve` the run succeeds, a person merges it and `decision` says shipped. `wf retry <run> implement --message "…"` is still accepted: `retryRefusal` returns null, the next tick files a new session and spends budget on a finished, merged run, and the run goes back to running, then awaiting approval. An ungated verified step on the same run is refused with `implement is verified: … nothing to try again`. No test covers this: run.test.ts:3082–3087 only tries `plan`, which has dependents. Suggested fix: count an approved step with no dependents as handed on. Add a test where a terminal gated step, once approved, refuses `wf retry --message`.

The gate refusal in `roundAsk` only fires when `budget === undefined`. `wf round <run> review --budget 5` on a looping step waiting at its gate (`again: false`) skips it. It falls through to line 1674, where `satisfiesAfter('awaiting approval')` is false, so the refusal says `round N is still running`. That is wrong: the round has ended and the step is waiting for approval. Without `--budget` the refusal correctly says to approve or send back. Dropping `budget === undefined` from the condition gives the right refusal in both cases.

Low priority, the person's call. findings.what: `Sighting.quietMs`'s doc still defines the field as "How long the session has been quiet — working, not busy, nothing written". After this change the claude runner sets `quietMs` on a sighting it reports with `busy: true` (runner.ts:1121), and that combination is exactly what now ends an attempt. This is the only place the engine states the runner↔engine contract — `decide` reads the field at domain.ts:481 and `closedOut` (engine.ts:111) still refuses to act on a busy statement — so the next reader, or the next runner written against this type, is told the one case that matters cannot happen. `QUIESCENT_AFTER_MS`'s doc at runner.ts:172 has the same stale clause ("How long `working` + not busy + nothing written must hold"), though the same constant is now also the busy rule's floor. The README and the `claudeOps` header both got the second rule; these two did not.

For a busy session whose transcript has been cold for the floor, `statementOf` runs on every pass: `keptRead` pins a read only when `FINAL.has(s.state)`, and this session's state is `working`, so it falls through to `read()` each time — a full `fs.readFile` of the transcript plus `jsonl.split('\n')` and a per-line scan, of a file the code's own comment (runner.ts:249) calls "tens of megabytes". The case is not rare: any tool call longer than 90s — `npm ci`, a build, this repo's own suite — leaves the session busy with a cold transcript for its whole length, so under `wf up`'s few-second tick that is the same multi-megabyte read and parse repeated for minutes, always returning the same answer. Previously a busy session cost nothing at all. The read is safely pinnable precisely because the condition being tested is that the transcript has not been written: the mtime + `MTIME_SLOP_MS` machinery `keptRead` already has would give one read per cold period instead of one per pass. If the cost is accepted instead, that is a judgement worth stating where the comment at runner.ts:1073 promises a busy session "costs its transcript's mtime and nothing more".

No test covers a retried ending against a held checkout, and README.md (`while a workspace: main task of any run on the same repository is unsettled, another is not filed`) and docs/features.md:2805 both state the rule in a form the code does not keep.

A cancelled run's ending task holds nothing while it is still in flight: the loop skips every `other.cancelledAt` run before it looks at the task's phase. `wf cancel` only asks the engine to stop the session; between that request and the engine settling the task as `stopped`, the ship agent is still mid `git merge` in the checkout, and the next tick files another run's approved ship into the same directory — two agents merging at once, the case the hold is for. Worth knowing that `slotWord` (`waiting for a run slot (…)`) already reads as `working` on the board for the same reason, so this is a second instance rather than a new kind of problem.

The `unheld` adjustment added to `decision`'s `statusOf` has no test that fails without it, so it could be deleted and the suite would stay green. findings.what: Stale files are removed only after every step's file is written, and a name counts as stale unless it matches exactly. On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS, or a repo on /mnt/c under WSL), renaming step `Review` to `review` goes wrong. `put('review.md')` reads or writes the existing `Review.md` entry. Then `Review.md` is not in `names`, so `rmSync` deletes that one file. The step's body is lost, the other steps' `after: review` now name no step, so the folder no longer loads, and the returned `steps` say it does. Removing stale files before writing, or comparing names case-folded, would fix it.

`e.isFile()` on a readdir Dirent is false for a symlink, but `loadWorkflows` reads a symlinked `old.md` as a step. If a folder has a symlinked step file that the save drops, the file is never removed. The folder then still reads that step, even though `steps` in the result leave it out. If that step waits on a step the save removed, the folder no longer loads, though the write reported success. And for a symlinked step file the save keeps, `fs.writeFileSync` (line 1052) writes through the link into whatever file it points at. Nobody links step files today (the api only documents linked folders), so this is low priority. It is still a gap in the promise that the folder reads back as the steps returned.

findings.what: `decision` returns `shipped` for any run that is not running and whose result branches are on the base branch, whatever its steps ended as. A result branch is cut at its run's base, so a terminal step that ended failed, blocked or unsigned with nothing committed leaves that branch on the base. `parentOf` asks `decision`, so the gate opens and the next tick files the child's roots, though no person has merged or decided anything. Its children start, and in a diamond the failure spreads down the graph, each run reading `shipped`. `wf decide` on that parent also prints `shipped — … is already on main` and hides the failure. That keeps the signed-off, nothing-to-commit parent that the store test ships.

summary: The four items do what was asked, and all three fixes from the last round are in with tests. The agent-workflows tests pass without turbo's cache (485 pass, 1 skipped) and typecheck is green. The run cap, item 31 and the queue are consistent across `wf tick`, `wf ls` and `wf decide`. Two small findings on the path where a queued card's start fails without a refusal: git's error is printed on every pass, and a daemon started after the failure never mentions the card. Both are worth a person's attention but not another round.

findings.what: The `git` helper calls `execFileSync` without `stdio`, so Node copies git's stderr to the process's own stderr as well as putting it in the error message. Before this change only a person's `wf start` reached it, once. Now `startQueued` (runner.ts:1244, via `startFromInbox` → `start` → `makeWorkspace`) retries a card that failed without a refusal on every pass. A queued card whose `repo:` is a folder with no git prints `fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git` on `wf up`'s terminal every 4 seconds, with no card name, for as long as it holds the queue. That contradicts the README's claim that `wf up` says it once. Running `node --test --test-name-pattern="fails without a refusal" test/queue-store.test.ts` shows four such lines for four passes. The test (queue-store.test.ts:563-577) only captures `console.log`, so it passes. Passing `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` to the helper keeps git's words in the error without the echo; a test that captures `process.stderr.write` over those passes would pin it.

`wf up` skips a queue line marked `again`, and `again` is judged against the try saved in `$WF_ROOT/queue/<name>.json` (runner.ts:1251), not against what this `wf up` process has printed. So a `wf up` started, or restarted, after the failure was written never names the card holding the queue: its first pass already reads `again: true`. queue-store.test.ts:574 pins exactly that, since its two `wf up` passes print nothing about `no-git-a1b2`, not even once. A person restarting the daemon to see why cards stopped starting gets no line about it; only `wf inbox` shows it. Remembering the last printed line in the `up` loop is presentation, not a decision the tick carries between passes, so it would not break the level-triggered rule.
